objections.claim: 'Known limitations' — a named element of every governing source — is absent from all six decided requirements. A matrix authored in full conformance with D-007 could omit limitations entirely and still satisfy the decided structure, contradicting the row D-007 claims to structure.
objections.evidence: DR-118's acceptance-evidence cell (file 08 line 281) names 'known limitations'. The source pin D-007 inherits (file 02 §Language-native product quality, lines 316-328) requires 'documented known limitations and unsupported tiers'. DR-G13's evidence column (file 08 line 327) names 'limitations'. The prototype reference's rule sentence (prototype-evidence-reference.md lines 32-35) names 'known limitations'. D-007's requirements 1-6 (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md lines 826-855): requirement 1's row contents are definition, prototype baseline or absence statement, V2 target, measurement method — no limitations cell; requirements 2-6 never mention limitations or unsupported tiers. Four independent sources name the element; the decided structure drops it. This is precisely the defect class D-007 exists to prevent: structure decided now so authoring cannot silently under-deliver the row.
objections.proposedFix: Add to requirement 1's row contents (or as a seventh requirement): each matrix row carries a known-limitations cell, and the matrix carries a role-level documented known-limitations and unsupported-tiers section, per file 02's own bullet. An empty limitations cell must be an explicit 'none known' statement, never blank — the same explicit-absence discipline requirement 1 already applies to missing prototype baselines.

objections.claim: The performance half of DR-118's 'behavior/performance baseline' element is covered by no decided requirement and routed to no named decision — and D-006 already punted the adjacent quantity (analyze RSS) to unnamed 'qualification-harness decisions', so per-capability performance baselines and targets currently belong nowhere. Silence here is the class the register forbids.
objections.evidence: DR-118 row: 'behavior/performance baseline'. File 02: 'behavior and performance baselines on supported platforms/corpora'. DR-G13: 'quality/performance measurements'. Prototype reference: 'record measured current and target behavior/performance'. D-007's capability enumeration (parse fidelity, semantic resolution, graph construction, finding classes, output projections) is purely functional; requirement 1's cells ('prototype-baseline measurement', 'V2 target (parity or named improvement)') never say performance, and no requirement names a runner class, workload dimension, or performance target discipline. D-006 (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md lines 755-759) deliberately excluded 'analyze' RSS from its thresholds — 'set by the qualification-harness decisions with product sign-off' — so the analyze-path performance surface has been explicitly deferred TO this row's neighborhood, and D-007 does not pick it up. D-001 condition-2 discipline: items excluded get explicit deferral dispositions, never silence (line 262-263).
objections.proposedFix: Either (a) add performance to the matrix structure: performance-bearing rows or columns carrying prototype-baseline measurement at the pinned commit on a named runner class (reuse D-006's reference-runner-class discipline and the D-002 platform set), a V2 target, and the same digest-pinned method; or (b) record an explicit routed deferral naming WHICH decision owns per-capability performance baselines/targets (e.g., the DR-G13/G14 harness-naming act with product sign-off, the D-006 pattern). Option silence is unlawful; the entry must choose and say so.

objections.claim: The decided matrix shape has no platform axis, but DR-G13's own evidence column defines the matrix as 'role × platform × digest-pinned corpus', and file 02 requires baselines 'on supported platforms/corpora'. D-002 fixed four platforms; a capability-rows-only matrix cannot express which cells are per-platform, so the decided shape under-specifies the gate it must discharge at.
objections.evidence: DR-G13 row (file 08 line 327): 'future product-selected role × platform × digest-pinned corpus matrix'. File 02 line 324: 'behavior and performance baselines on supported platforms/corpora'. D-002 (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md lines 429-430): platforms macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux x86_64/arm64. D-007 requirement 1 decides 'one row per analysis capability' with four named cells and no platform dimension anywhere in requirements 1-6. Item 6 discharges the evidence half at 'DR-G13/G14 qualification' — i.e., at a gate whose evidence column demands a dimension the decided structure omits.
objections.proposedFix: State the platform axis: the matrix binds to the D-002 platform set; declare per cell class whether it is per-platform (performance, refusal/containment behavior) or platform-invariant (semantic/graph goldens), with platform-invariance itself an explicit recorded claim per row, not a default. This is structure, not authoring — exactly D-007's remit.

objections.claim: D-007 is silent on the parked-identity rides, breaking consistency with adopted D-002. File 02 requires 'language-specific semantic, identity, Coverage, graph, and failure goldens' — identity and Coverage goldens structurally depend on DR-006-parked recipes, and the quantifier 'capability the role advertises' leans on a capability-manifest surface whose identity (capabilityManifestId) is itself a DR-006-named gap. Authoring those goldens under D-007's structure as written would settle parked identity semantics by prose — the exact thing D-002's symmetry clause forbids.
objections.evidence: File 02 line 323: 'language-specific semantic, identity, Coverage, graph, and failure goldens' (identity and Coverage named as required golden classes for DR-118). File 08 'Exact DR-006 park coverage' (lines 57-67): finding fingerprint, RunId, FactViewId, subjectScopeCommitment parked; 'Related named gaps are policyOutcome.derivationDigest and capabilityManifestId'; typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot recorded as PlanId-affecting with no producing rule — the TypeScript role specifically. D-002's Identity-dependencies section (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md lines 368-397): SARIF-for-analyze rides the fingerprint/RunId recipes; Coverage-on-TS-dispatch rides subjectScopeCommitment; PlanId-for-TS rides typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot; and the symmetry clause — every dependent feature 'ships reduced, re-scoped, or waits, by that disposition's terms; none of them survives on prose'. D-007 (lines 815-862) never mentions DR-006, identity, Coverage, fingerprints, or rides. Its output-projections capability row and any golden keyed by finding identity inherit these parks unnamed.
objections.proposedFix: Add the D-002-pattern clause as a decided requirement: matrix rows and golden classes whose measurement method depends on parked identity recipes — at minimum identity goldens, Coverage goldens, the output-projections/SARIF row, and any PlanId-dependent measurement (typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot) — carry a NAMED ride on the DR-006 closure; if DR-006 closes by scoped disposition rather than binding recipes, those rows re-scope by that disposition's terms. Name the ride, never pretend it settled.

objections.claim: Requirement 5 truncates the no-silent-fallback enumeration to two of the named fallback targets. The prototype reference forbids silent fallback to 'a weaker parser, syntactic tier, graph, or finding model'; file 02 to 'a weaker syntactic, semantic, or graph answer'. D-007 decides the negative-test class as refusing degradation 'to a weaker parser/syntactic tier' only — so graph-degradation, semantic-degradation and finding-model-degradation fallbacks escape the required test class in the decided bytes, narrowing DR-G13's rule while claiming to adopt it.
objections.evidence: prototype-evidence-reference.md lines 37-38: 'No role may silently fall back to a weaker parser, syntactic tier, graph, or finding model.' File 02 lines 327-328: 'tests proving there is no silent fallback to a weaker syntactic, semantic, or graph answer.' D-007 requirement 5 (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md lines 848-852): 'REFUSES (typed, loud) rather than degrading to a weaker parser/syntactic tier when its capability is unavailable' — two members where the sources name four (union: parser, syntactic tier, semantic, graph, finding model).
objections.proposedFix: Quantify over the full class: for each capability, a negative test that the role refuses (typed, loud) rather than silently degrading to ANY weaker answer — parser, syntactic tier, semantic, graph, or finding model, per the prototype reference's and file 02's own enumerations — with the enumeration cited by reference so a future widening of the source rule widens the test class automatically.

objections.claim: Requirement 1's parenthetical capability list is ambiguous between a closed enumeration and an example list, and both readings are defective: closed risks the DR-011-R12 class (omissions decided before the authoring that would reveal them, and overreach into the matrix authoring D-007 expressly disclaims); open makes 'one row per capability the role advertises' unfalsifiable, because no pinned surface defines what the role 'advertises' — the capability-manifest identity is a DR-006-named gap and file 01 defines advertisement only for SARIF-emitting commands.
objections.evidence: D-007 requirement 1: 'one row per analysis capability the role advertises (parse fidelity, semantic resolution, graph construction, finding classes, output projections)' — no floor/ceiling marker. 'What this does NOT do: author the matrix or corpus' (line 856-857). File 08 DR-006 park coverage: 'capabilityManifestId' is a named gap; the same section supplies the corpus's own cure for exactly this shape of problem: 'The property—not this enumeration—is the boundary; refresh must search for all members and cannot close only the listed rows.' File 01 line 116 defines 'advertises' only for SARIF ('a command or installed reporting capability advertises SARIF'); no per-role capability-advertisement surface is pinned anywhere D-007 cites.
objections.proposedFix: Adopt the DR-006 construction: declare the parenthetical an illustrative FLOOR (rows that must exist), declare the quantifier the boundary, and bind the quantifier to a named derivation source — the host-contract capability declarations the role registers plus the prototype reference's role/capability inventory table — with a completeness derivation (enumerating the advertised set from pinned bytes) required as part of matrix acceptance. That keeps the row set falsifiable without authoring it now.

objections.claim: The prototype reference's missing-baseline rule is adopted by half. Requirement 1 takes the explicit-absence statement but drops (a) the 'inapplicable' case and (b) the replacement rule — a missing/inapplicable prototype baseline is 'replaced only by a product-approved language-native corpus'. As decided, a row may state 'no prototype baseline exists' and then ground its V2 target in nothing at all; requirement 3's 'ONLY admissible existing-behavior reference' phrasing makes this worse by appearing to foreclose the replacement path the source rule requires.
objections.evidence: prototype-evidence-reference.md lines 35-37: 'A missing or inapplicable prototype baseline must be stated explicitly and replaced only by a product-approved language-native corpus.' D-007 requirement 1: 'or an explicit "no prototype baseline exists" statement per the prototype reference's own rule' — the absence half only; 'inapplicable' unhandled. Requirement 3: prototype at a62509d6 'is the ONLY admissible "existing behavior" reference' — true against unpinned recollections, but unqualified it collides with the source rule's replacement clause.
objections.proposedFix: Complete the adoption: 'missing OR INAPPLICABLE' baseline stated explicitly, and when stated, the row's target grounds in a product-approved language-native corpus per the prototype reference's replacement rule; requirement 3 rephrased as 'the only admissible PROTOTYPE-behavior reference' so it excludes recollections without contradicting the lawful replacement path.

objections.claim: D-007 records no alternatives-considered and no rationale section, violating D-000 clause 3 and this file's own entry format — and the omission hides a real preference trade a product owner could take the other way. Preference honesty (the D-002 baseline/ratchet precedent) requires the trade recorded in bytes.
objections.evidence: COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md lines 9-12 (entry format: 'decision, alternatives considered, rationale, reviewer + verdict + digest...') and D-000 clause 3 (lines 36-38). D-007 contains Date, Status, Decision type, Decided requirements, What-this-does-NOT-do, Overturn, Reviewer, Commit — no alternatives, no rationale header. The live alternatives: (a) a THINNER slice-1 matrix — rows at the prototype inventory's granularity (prototype-evidence-reference.md role table) with per-capability granularity deferred to qualification; cheaper authoring, weaker falsifiability; (b) thresholds decided NOW — a blanket parity-with-prototype default with named exceptions — rather than product approval at matrix acceptance; earlier falsifiability, at the risk of numbers without workloads (the exact ground D-006 used to exclude analyze RSS). D-002 recorded its equivalent trade 'in bytes' (T2-02, lines 421-427); D-007 records neither alternative nor why the chosen point beats them.
objections.proposedFix: Add an alternatives-considered/rationale section naming (a) and (b), the trade each takes, and why the chosen structure (full per-capability granularity now, numeric thresholds at acceptance) wins — presumably: granularity is cheap to decide and expensive to retrofit, while numbers without a corpus repeat the mistake D-006 refused.

objections.claim: The DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED reuse is lawful on precedent, but the annotation must name the still-undecided preference half. D-006 already stretched the label's definition ('required accepted successor remains missing' read as the missing evidence half) for DR-115 — a V2 row in the same table — under three-turn consent, and its turn-2 NOTE-03 keeps the status vocabulary closed, so reuse is the lawful option and coining an analog would itself be a register-content decision. The material difference: D-115's annotation says 'thresholds DECIDED' because D-006 decided actual numbers; D-007 decides structure only, with per-row thresholds still awaiting product approval at matrix acceptance. An unqualified 'DECIDED' annotation would overclaim relative to the DR-115 precedent it mirrors.
objections.evidence: File 08 lines 26-27 (label definition), line 278 (DR-115 row carrying the label with the measurement-half annotation, D-006 precedent landed in bytes), line 281 (DR-118 row). D-006 turn-2 NOTE-03 (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md lines 719-721). D-007 item 6: 'role list (D-002) and acceptance structure (this entry) DECIDED; the matrix/corpus evidence half is discharged at DR-G13/G14 qualification' — accurate as far as it goes, but silent that the per-row parity/improvement thresholds (requirement 4) remain an UNDECIDED product approval, unlike DR-115 where the numbers themselves were decided.
objections.proposedFix: Extend item 6's row annotation: '...acceptance structure (D-007) DECIDED; per-row thresholds remain product approvals at matrix acceptance (D-007 req 4); the matrix/corpus evidence half is discharged at DR-G13/G14 qualification.' One clause; the label then claims exactly what is decided, no more.

objections.claim: Requirement 3 cites DR-203's verification of the prototype pin without carrying that verdict's recorded caveats: the pin is SHA-1 commit identity, and custody is a sibling clone outside the corpus. A structure that makes this pin the sole admissible behavior reference should require measurement records to re-verify commit identity at measurement time, or the matrix inherits a trust root the corpus itself flagged.
objections.evidence: File 08 DR-203 row (line 300): 'SHA-1-identity and out-of-corpus-custody caveats recorded' — the verification found every named file present at a62509d6 in the sibling opensip-cli clone, with those two caveats explicit. D-007 requirement 3 cites 'verified available and byte-checked by the DR-203 re-review' and stops; nothing in the decided structure obliges a baseline measurement to record that it re-verified the clone stands at the pinned commit when the measurement ran.
objections.proposedFix: Add one clause to requirement 3: every prototype-baseline measurement records the commit-identity re-verification of the clone it measured against (and the two DR-203 caveats travel with the citation), so a drifted or substituted clone cannot silently feed baseline cells.

summaryForCoordinator: OBJECTIONS: 5 MUST-FIX, 3 SHOULD-FIX, 2 NOTE. The structure's frame is sound (structure-now/evidence-later, the DR-115 pattern), but the decided requirements drop named elements of every governing source: known limitations (01), the performance half plus its D-006-orphaned analyze surface (02), DR-G13's platform axis (03), the DR-006 identity/Coverage-golden rides D-002's symmetry clause requires named (04), and two of four forbidden fallback targets (05). The capability enumeration needs the DR-006 'property-not-enumeration' construction to be falsifiable without authoring (06); the missing-baseline replacement rule is half-adopted (07); alternatives/rationale are absent contra D-000 clause 3 (08). Label reuse is lawful on the D-006 precedent with one honesty clause (09); the prototype-pin caveats should travel (10).
